newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 24.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 24.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Consumers in Britain are complaining more about cross-border advertising than people in other European countries, while, ironically, ads created in Britain are coming under the most fire across Europe, according to figures released by the European Advertising Standards Alliance.
PARIS - French advertising agency Publicis says it has formed a top management team of three at its FCA!BMZ network in a move aimed at emphasising the unit's European orientation.

LONDON - British cider maker Matthew Clark, whose share of the cider market has fallen in the face of booming "alcopop" sales says it has sharply increased advertising for the new financial year to 9.0 million pounds from 2.0 million for its key Diamond White and Blackthorn brand ciders, as well as the launch of Blackthorn Gold.
MUNICH - British airline Britannia Airways Ltd awards its press and public relations account for its German unit to the Munich-based PR agency Wilde & Partner, the agency says.

WASHINGTON - The government says that Quaker State Corp has settled charges that it falsely advertised that Blue Coral "Slick 50" engine treatment would reduce engine wear. The ads have been discontinued.
FRANKFURT - Ad agency Buehler & Partner says it has won the European-wide account for radiator brand Stelrad.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LOS ANGELES - Magician David Copperfield claimed $30 million damages from Paris Match magazine for alleging his romance with supermodel Claudia Schiffer was a sham. His defamation suit, filed in Los Angeles Superior Court against the French magazine's publishers and a rival magician, Herbert Becker, said the claim was false. *********

FRANKFURT - The 50 largest German publishing houses boosted turnover by nearly eight percent last year fuelled by strong growth among the top three companies, trade magazine Horizont says. Revenues jumped 7.9 percent to 59.5 billion marks during 1996, with media company Bertelsmannleading the industry by a wide margin.

AMSTERDAM - Music and film group PolyGram NV says it will take a careful approach to the Internet but is looking at the opportunities for expanding record sales by moving beyond the traditional retail outlets.

LUDWIGSHAFEN, Germany - The association of state media authorities calls for the agreement over digital television between CLT-Ufa, the Kirch group and Deutsche Telekom to be made public. The authorities say the information is particularly important for private cable companies and programming providers.
MADRID - Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica says that a firm deal to buy a stake in television channel Antena 3 has not been reached and talks are ongoing.
LONDON - Shares in Britain's three largest commercial TV companies rise on proposals to base more of their licence fees on revenue rather than a fixed fee.

LONDON - British companies say they are becoming more confident about using the Internet to ply their trade because of ever-improving solutions devised by the industry to ward off intruders and ensure security, say industry experts.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - French mobile phone companies sold record numbers of portable phones in June thanks to special offers designed to reach the general public, the firms say.

NEW YORK - International Business Machines Corp announces a reorganisation of some of its major businesses and key executive changes, moves analysts say seem to be aimed at improving sluggish hardware results.
WASHINGTON - Daimler-Benz AG expects U.S. sales to make up 25 percent of total revenue within the next five years, up from 20 percent at present, chief executive Juergen Schrempp says.
MELBOURNE - Foster's Brewing Group Ltd says it expects Philip Morris Cos Inc to sell its 20-percent stake in Canada's Molson Breweries to both Foster's and Molson Cos Ltd.

PRAGUE - New passenger car sales in the Czech Republic rose in the first half of 1997 to 89,795 from 74,792 while imports rose to 40,081 from 32,804, compared with the same period of 1996, the Czech Car Importers Association says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

SINGAPORE - Wealthy Singapore's latest idea to prevent the tiny island from being submerged by cars has not won much of a welcome from motorists. A pay-as-you-use Road Pricing Scheme has been introduced to ease rush-hour congestion on the busiest stretches of roads as the number of cars goes on rising.
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg has launched a two billion rand ($440 million) project to claw back the city centre from the ravages of crime and grime to attract businesses back to the City.

LJUBLJANA, Slovenia - Tourists are returning to Slovenian holiday resorts since the end of the war in the former Yugoslavia. Visitors in the first six months of the year increased by nine percent compared to the same period in 1996, the Slovenian Statistical Office says.

BONN - Germans bought more beverages last year than in 1995, says the association of refreshments manufacturers. The industry group says turnover grew by 2.9 percent last year and production increased by 2.1 percent.
